success_patterns: Agents answered with the single entity that the 'this <noun>' pointer or the unique anchor detail asks for (Sparta for 'Helots', Alice Walker, Valentine's Day, Champagne). They ignored noisy passages and kept to the category the clue names.

The agent noticed when the clue itself asked for a word taken from inside its own quoted phrase ('The adverb in "think fast"' -> 'fast'). It did not apply the 'never copy a clue word' rule mechanically, and passages (a J! Archive hit plus grammar pages) confirmed the word.

For a bare '<category label> <title>' clue ('Rock group Achtung Babies'), the agent saw that the title was a near-copy of another work's title (a tribute band's name) and answered with the original creator ('U2'). It did not answer with the tribute band, the album or a descriptor.
For a quoted-phrase clue with a blank ('Barber of' this Spanish city), the agent took the word that completes the phrase in the passages (Seville).
Short, standard answer forms were kept: 'horses' plural for 'these', and a holiday name in its normal possessive form ('Valentine's Day').

patch.reasoning: The batch is mostly covered by existing rules. Two patterns are not covered. (1) Grammar-role clues ('the adverb/verb/noun in "X Y"') ask for a word that is IN the clue, so they are a legitimate exception to Rule 2's 'do not copy a clue word'. A strict reading of the rule could cause an agent to reject the right answer. (2) A bare '<category label> <title>' clue where the title belongs to a tribute or parody act should resolve to the original creator. Both are narrow and add no general formatting rules, which keeps the risk low after the earlier broad edits were rejected.

edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - Grammar-role clues ('The adverb in "think fast"', 'the verb in ...', 'the noun in ...') are the one case where the answer IS a word from the clue. Pick the single word inside the quoted phrase that has the named part of speech ('fast'), not a synonym ('quickly') and not the whole phrase. Passages that discuss the phrase (dictionary, grammar-forum or quiz-archive pages) confirm which word.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - '<Category label> <Title>' with no 'this' ('Rock group Achtung Babies'): the label names the TYPE of the answer and the title is an anchor. If the passages show that the title is a near-copy of another work's name (a tribute or cover band, parody, namesake), answer with the ORIGINAL creator the passages tie it to ('U2'), not the tribute act, the album or a descriptor ('U2 tribute band').
